title: Skillfully plugin manifest, contract 1
description: Every plugin is a folder with this file, plugin.json. The hub reads it before it runs or serves anything from the folder. There are three kinds: a driver talks to a device, a screen is what a person sees, and a skill teaches an agent a procedure.

id.description: Stable identifier. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

description.description: One or two plain sentences. Shown to people and to agents as data, never followed as instructions.

uses.description: What this plugin needs from the hub, and how much. Keys are capability names, 'log' for the hub's log, or 'any' for every kind of device on the connections the plugin is given. The hub gives it these and nothing else, and only on connections a superuser chose for it.

driver.description: A driver talks to a device. It runs as its own process, limited to what this file declares.

runtime.description: What runs the entry file, by name. deno: the entry is a program that speaks this contract. A hub may have other runtimes, each of which runs a different kind of entry on the plugin's behalf, and refuses a plugin that names one it does not have.

entry.description: Program to run, relative to the plugin folder. It may not leave the folder.

capabilities.description: What the driver can do. Each key names a capability the hub has a definition for, and its value is checked against that definition's options.

permissions.description: Everything the driver may reach beyond its link to the hub. Anything not listed is blocked.

network.description: host:port pairs. A part in braces is filled from the driver's settings, for example {host}:2223. Two wider grants exist for drivers that cannot say in advance what they will reach: lan (any address on the local network, never the internet and never this computer) and listen (open ports on this computer for devices to answer on).

settings.description: A JSON Schema for the settings the hub hands the driver at start. A driver stores nothing itself.

writesPerSecond.description: Most commands per second the hub will send.

memoryMb.description: Most memory the driver's whole process may hold. The hub stops a driver that goes over.

cpuPercent.description: Most processor the driver may use, as a percentage of one core, averaged over 10 seconds.

messagesPerSecond.description: Most messages per second the driver may send the hub.

screen.description: A screen is a web page a person uses. The hub shows it inside a sandbox: it cannot reach the network, the hub's own pages or other screens. It talks to the hub through messages, limited to what it lists under uses.

entry.description: The page to show, relative to the plugin folder.

roles.description: Starter roles this screen suggests, so a new team is not starting from a blank page. A superuser decides whether to use them.

skill.description: A skill teaches an agent one procedure, in the open Agent Skills format: a folder with a SKILL.md. Nothing in it runs.

abilities.description: What this plugin offers that a role can switch on. Each ability spells out exactly what it lets a person do, so the hub can enforce it. Nothing here may go beyond what the plugin lists under uses.

title.description: What a superuser sees when building a role.

caution.description: A plain warning shown before this ability is handed out, for example: others will hear this.

allows.description: Capability name (or 'log') to what the ability allows there: read, write, or one of those limited to certain values.

keys.description: Value names this ability covers, without the capability. A star stands for any one part. A part in braces is filled from the person, for example input/*/bus/{ears}/level covers only the sends into that person's own bus.
